display.purpose: "The Lobby" on the public welcome only.

display-lead.purpose: The "Welcome to" line over the display name.

headline.purpose: The centred VIP Lobby title on navy, inside the marquee.

title.purpose: The base section-title scale; the VIP Lobby's "Your Tools" and "Admin Tools" labels run smaller (1.25rem, 650). The identity mark is a near sibling.

card-title.purpose: Tool names on VIP tiles (15ch measure); the launch screen sets the opened Tool's name in the same lettering at twice the size.

lead.purpose: The welcome purpose line (34ch measure); the lobby lead and guidance lines run smaller (1.1875rem, 600).

state.purpose: A Minecraft world's state ("Ready to join"), the biggest words in its column; Foundry's state in its status card.

value.purpose: A connection value to copy; it wraps after its dots and colons, and only a part too long for its line breaks inside it. The Launcher's world columns, the only place one appears now, set it at 1.375rem.

hint.purpose: Where a device tab plays, under its label.

shadows.name: tactile-base
shadows.purpose: Coral base and soft navy drop under every custard tactile control; --lift is 0.75rem hero, 0.5rem default, 0.3rem small.

shadows.name: tactile-base-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover and focus-visible: face lifts 2px, base deepens.

shadows.name: tactile-base-active
shadows.purpose: Pressed: face sinks onto the base.

shadows.name: ground-shadow
shadows.purpose: The flat navy footprint at 22% alpha: the ellipse under the robot host and the footprints under the Tool miniatures (Soccer's pitch, Foundry's tabletop, each Launcher plot). It also colours the Launcher board's drop.

shadows.name: board-drop
shadows.purpose: The soft drop under the Minecraft Launcher's board, the one panel that casts a shadow.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The house easing (expo ease-out): state transitions, the tile rise, the launch screen, and the fallback for the selector's glide. On the Minecraft Launcher it carries the rows' settle, the device marker, the copy feedback, the status glyph's change, the plots' arrival and parts of the plots' one-shots (EXPO_OUT in minecraft/plots/stage.ts). The cabinet adds its own sampled glide and spring (the Launcher's plots and custard rise reuse the spring), and the glyph and host moves shape each keyframe with their own curves, as some plot moves do.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.value: 160ms
motion.purpose: Hover/focus transitions on tactile and quiet controls.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.value: 60ms
motion.purpose: Tactile active (press) response.

motion.name: duration-arrow
motion.value: 200ms
motion.purpose: Hero arrow nudge on hover.

motion.name: robot-wave
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-out) after 0.5s, once
motion.purpose: The host's single wave on welcome arrival, and on the Minecraft Launcher once each time a status answer shows a world turning ready while the page is open, never on arrival. The other Tool footers are static; the VIP Lobby's host moves only with the cabinet (host-greet, host-jump).

motion.name: status-dots
motion.value: 1.1s var(--ease-out) infinite, 0.15s stagger
motion.purpose: The house loading dots beside a waiting line: checking access in the VIP Lobby, the Minecraft Launcher and Minecraft Admin, Soccer's loading lines, and Foundry's first check in place of its status mark. The VIP launch screen fades them in under the Tool's name after 900ms.

motion.name: status-turn
motion.value: 1.4s linear infinite
motion.purpose: The busy arrow beside a Minecraft world's state while that world is starting (from the press of its Start) or stopping, and Foundry's while a fresh reading says it is starting or shutting down. It and the loading dots loop for as long as their wait lasts; nothing else loops, and the VIP marquee's chase is cut off by its timer.

motion.name: tool-stamp
motion.value: 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: Soccer's decorative calendar check settles from scale 1.2 to 1 when a Team is selected. Disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: glide
motion.value: --glide-tl / --glide-tr / --glide-bl / --glide-br: 480ms linear(...) per corner, sampled by cabinet.ts glide(travel, 4) (25 stops, samples = 24, of a damped spring peaking halfway; overshoot min(8%, max(0.2%, 4px / travel))); fallback var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The VIP selector's per-move glide: each corner settles at most 4px past the tile however far it travels, even when a move cuts into the last one. Corners on the side it travels toward lead by up to 50ms (--lead-*).

motion.name: selector-appear
motion.value: opacity 160ms var(--ease-out); close in from 14px out, let go 7px out
motion.purpose: The selector appears by closing in on the first picked tile and lets go outward as it fades when the pointer leaves the cabinet and no tile has focus.

motion.name: spring-loose
motion.purpose: The control deck's joystick: pushed in 130ms on var(--ease-out), let go 140ms after the push begins, then springs back upright over 620ms with about 13% overshoot. Leans up to 22°. The Minecraft Launcher's plots and its custard rise (380ms) run on the same sampled curve, kept as SPRING in minecraft/plots/stage.ts.

motion.name: marquee-chase
motion.value: 105ms a step, 3 phases (315ms cycle), step-end; 1300ms on a pick, 2400ms on the Tools' arrival
motion.purpose: The VIP marquee's clockwise chase. Removed by its timer, so nothing loops at rest.

motion.name: marquee-flash
motion.value: 340ms step-end x2
motion.purpose: Pressing Open flashes every marquee bulb twice; a second press switches to twin keyframes to restart it.

motion.name: deck-press
motion.value: 70ms var(--ease-out); cap sinks 3.5px and fills custard
motion.purpose: The deck's first drawn button while Open is pressed; lets up 220ms after a press that never became a click.

motion.name: tile-pick
motion.value: background-color 140ms var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The picked VIP tile fills with limb.

motion.name: tile-rise
motion.value: 420ms var(--ease-out), 45ms stagger in reading order; from translateY(0.75rem) scale(0.96)
motion.purpose: VIP tiles rise into place as the Member's Tools arrive, fully drawn from the first frame (no fade).

motion.name: glyph-calendar
motion.value: page flips over its binding 520ms (scaleY 1 to 0.03 to 1.07 to 1); its two rings lift 2px and drop back within the same 520ms, cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.7, 0.4, 1); six days pop to 1.3x over 260ms ease-out from 300ms, 40ms apart (about 760ms in all)
motion.purpose: Soccer's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-cube
motion.value: 720ms: squat, hop 5px while turning around (scaleX 1 to -1), squashed landing
motion.purpose: Minecraft Launcher's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-foundry
motion.value: 560ms: lift 3px at 1.14x, stamp to scale(1.12, 0.84), settle
motion.purpose: Foundry's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-gear
motion.value: 760ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); rotate 90deg (two teeth)
motion.purpose: Admin glyphs turn their gear on each pick. A glyph move already running finishes first.

motion.name: host-greet
motion.value: 620ms ease-out hop (5px, then 1.5px); arm waves 1200ms ease-in-out after 120ms
motion.purpose: The VIP footer's 40px host greets a pick, only when 12 seconds have passed since the last pick.

motion.name: host-jump
motion.value: 560ms squash-and-jump (9px); arm raises 640ms ease-in-out; restarts on each press
motion.purpose: The host jumps when Open is pressed.

motion.name: launch
motion.value: starts 90ms after the click; 560ms var(--ease-out) clip-path inset(... round 14px) from the tile's box past the screen's edges; field fill tile to seafoam; loading dots fade in 240ms after 900ms; hands the lobby back after 8000ms without a navigation
motion.purpose: The VIP launch screen grows from the opened tile while the browser loads the Tool; the link navigates at once and the screen only decorates the wait.

motion.name: plot-arrive
motion.value: 420ms var(--ease-out) backwards, 60ms stagger in the board's order; from translateY(0.5rem)
motion.purpose: The Launcher's plots rise into place as the worlds arrive, fully drawn in their true state from the first frame (no fade). No control moves with them. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: plot-moves
motion.value: one-shots, each part on its own curve (the plots' spring, which is the --spring-loose samples, var(--ease-out), the plain easing keywords and a few curves of their own), by plot: Start pressed 430 to 700ms; turning ready after starting 2000 to 2580ms (1220ms for the fallback server block); found ready any other way 500 to 1040ms; a stop beginning 600 to 760ms and ending 320 to 640ms; a failed start 380 to 700ms. The plain block of a backend that lists no worlds has no flag, so it takes 940ms turning ready, 420ms found ready any other way and 220ms as a stop begins
motion.purpose: The Launcher's plots move from one state's picture to the next, each answering something that happened: Start pressed, the world turning ready (the one big moment, as the host waves; the plot's one custard light comes on here, never before), a stop beginning and ending, and a start that didn't take. A newer state cuts a move still running; off screen, in a hidden tab and under reduced motion the plot simply shows its new picture.

motion.name: plot-beat
motion.value: 400ms (420ms for the fallback server block), once per status answer the page shows
motion.purpose: One small beat on the plot while its world is starting or stopping, so the plot moves only when the page hears back. It never loops, never cuts a move still playing and never suggests measured progress; skipped off screen, in a hidden tab and under reduced motion.

motion.name: plot-flare
motion.value: 420ms ease-out, once: the plot's one light swells (flame 1.16x, site lamp 1.25x, block lamp 1.28x); on the Gatehouse the lit doorway holds while its rays push out to 1.4x and the pennant flicks
motion.purpose: The ready world's address reaching the clipboard: its plot's light flares once. Only while the world is ready and no other move is playing; skipped off screen, in a hidden tab and under reduced motion.

motion.name: status-mark-change
motion.value: opacity 160ms, transform 260ms, stroke-dashoffset 280ms and fill 160ms, all var(--ease-out); the moon, arrow, bang and question enter from scale(0.6); the tick draws on after a 140ms delay
motion.purpose: The Launcher's status glyph turns one mark into the next on a change of state: the block's outline unwinds as the busy arrow takes over, and the tick draws itself on the filled block. The marks swap at once under reduced motion; the state's words always sit beside it.

motion.name: row-settle
motion.value: 360ms var(--ease-out) on grid-template-rows (height for the lead), from the old row heights to the new; only when a row differs by more than 0.5px; while it runs every row of a world but its plot-and-name row, and the two blocks under the board (the steps and Before you join), are stretched to their tracks and cut 0.75rem outside their edges (clip-path: inset(-0.75rem)); at 45rem and under, Before you join is cut lower at its foot, 0.65rem + 7px below it, so its link's target and focus ring stay whole; the lead is cut at its own edge
motion.purpose: The Launcher's rows glide to a new height when a world's state, a Stop question, a notice or the device changes what they hold: the board's own rows side by side, each world's when stacked, and the lead above and the steps under it. Words and controls change at once. Never on arrival; a change of window width cuts it; a second change carries on from where the first had got to; off screen, in a hidden tab or under reduced motion the board simply changes.

motion.name: marker-travel
motion.value: leading edge 280ms var(--ease-out); trailing edge 280ms var(--ease-out) after 35ms; the edges are registered <length> properties (--mc-marker-l, --mc-marker-r) clipping one 4px seafoam rule
motion.purpose: The Launcher's device tabs share one underline, which stretches toward a newly chosen tab and gathers under it, on the same pixels as a tab's own underline. It is simply moved when the bar changes shape, where the properties can't be registered, and under reduced motion; until the tabs are measured the chosen tab draws its own underline.

motion.name: custard-rise
motion.value: held flat for 220ms (translateY(var(--lift)), the coral base at 0, the drop at 0 alpha), then 380ms up onto its base on the plots' spring (the --spring-loose samples, about 13% overshoot); --lift is 0.5rem on Start and 0.3rem on Copy address
motion.purpose: A custard control that becomes the thing to press while the Launcher is open (Copy address as its world turns ready, Start when a world can be started again) rises once its row has all but settled, so the depth that means "press me" arrives as a move. Never on arrival; a press, a key or a newer state cuts it; skipped off screen, in a hidden tab and under reduced motion.

motion.name: copied-line
motion.value: in: from translateY(100%), 240ms var(--ease-out), backwards; out ("copied" only): colour to transparent over 260ms ease-in, ending as the line clears at 4000ms
motion.purpose: What a copy came to slides up into the feedback line under that world's values from the line's foot, fully drawn; "copied" lets go over its last quarter second, and a copy that has to be done by hand stays until the next copy in that world's column, a change of device, or a change in that world's address or port. The line keeps room for one line of words, so "copied" moves no row; a message long enough to wrap makes its row taller at once. No slide or fade under reduced motion.

motion.name: switch-slide
motion.value: knob: transform 120ms ease-out, 1.375rem to the right; track: background-color 120ms ease-out, pale seafoam to navy
motion.purpose: Minecraft Admin's switch as a mod is turned on or off. It uses the plain ease-out keyword, not the house curve. The slide stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; }
motion.purpose: All CSS motion off under prefers-reduced-motion. The cabinet's scripted moves (glyph moves, marquee, joystick, host, launch) never start: the selector still marks the picked tile without travelling, and Open simply navigates. The Minecraft Launcher's scripted moves (the plots' one-shots, the rows' settle, the custard rise) never start either: the board and its plots simply change.

narrative.overview:
The Lobby looks like the title screen of a friendly couch co-op game: a matte seafoam field, deep navy lettering and outlines, and one fat custard button sitting on a coral base, waiting to be pressed. Everything is drawn as flat, outlined shapes in a small palette, the way a cartoon game menu is drawn, and the depth that exists is physical (a button you press down) rather than atmospheric.

The public welcome is a single title menu with giant centred lettering, one action, a low custard sun, and layered seafoam foliage. A small robot host waves once beside the navy ground wave. The signed-in VIP Lobby uses **Arcade Cabinet**, selected by Craig on 2026-11-11, and **Attract Mode**, chosen the same day to bring it to life. The title is centred inside a marquee of bulbs on the navy field above a pale seafoam cabinet. Each seafoam Tool tile acts as a launch key, with a navy glyph, a full Tool name, and a custard Open control. Picking a tile closes a navy selector around it and plays its glyph's move; pressing Open grows the tile into a launch screen while the Tool loads. A seafoam control deck with a joystick and two buttons sits under the cabinet. The launcher keeps the robot at 40px in its navy footer.

Tool interiors share a blocky world drawn in those same materials: isometric miniatures, navy number tiles, framed controls and a stepped navy ground. Minecraft has a plot for each world, Soccer a pitch and calendar, and Foundry a tabletop scene. Each drawing belongs to its task and leaves the working controls in reach.

Navy does every structural job (type, outlines, rules, glyphs, focus rings, the ground). Custard is the action and drawn light (the welcome's sun, the one light on each Minecraft plot). Coral is the tactile base and the robot's body, never text. Seafoam and its lighter tints are the field and the surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Matte seafoam field with navy type and navy outlines on everything drawn.
One tactile control: custard face, navy outline, coral base, sinks when pressed.
Rounded, chunky lettering (Rubik) over a soft, readable text face (Nunito Sans).
Flat surfaces separated by 2px navy outlines and 1.5px navy rules, not by shadow.
Hand-drawn SVG scenery and a robot host, all in the token palette, all decorative.
One task-specific miniature per Tool interior, drawn in the Lobby's own block materials, with shared number tiles and stepped ground.

rules.name: The Navy Does the Drawing Rule
rules.body: Outlines, rules and glyph strokes stay navy. Text and focus rings are navy on light surfaces; on navy regions, text flips to seafoam-light with seafoam supporting copy, footer links and focus rings turn custard.

rules.name: The One Thing to Press Rule
rules.body: Custard on a coral base means "press me". Do not use custard as a surface fill for cards, panels or banners, and do not use coral for anything that is not a tactile base or the robot. Outside the tactile control, custard appears only as drawn light: the welcome's sun, the Minecraft plots' lights and the tabletop lamp, the VIP marquee's lit bulbs, and the control deck's first button while Open is pressed. The deck's buttons are drawn, never pressable, so they stay pale at rest.

rules.name: The Heavy Menu Rule
rules.body: Headings run tight (negative tracking from -0.005em to -0.025em, line-height at or under 1.05) and balanced. Body text never goes tight.

rules.name: The Semibold Voice Rule
rules.body: Short functional sentences on the field (purpose, lead, guidance, notices, status) are Nunito Sans 600, so they hold up on saturated seafoam. Long running text stays at 400.

rules.name: The Only Pressable Thing Has Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth means "this can be pressed". Cards, panels, notices and the quiet button stay flat; the coral base and its lift belong to the tactile control alone.

dos: **Do** draw every line, letter, outline and glyph in navy; flip to seafoam-light text and custard links and focus rings on the navy ground.
**Do** make the primary action the custard tactile control with its coral base, and keep one per view at hero size.
**Do** separate cards and panels with 2px navy outlines on 1rem corners (0.875rem for the VIP Lobby's Tool tiles), and page regions with 1.5px navy rules.
**Do** draw new Tool glyphs in the existing stroke family: 32px grid, 2.5px navy stroke, round joins; admin variants add the corner gear.

**Do** keep sun, foliage and ground wave on the public welcome. Give Tool interiors their shared block world and task-specific miniature. Keep every illustration and the robot decorative and aria-hidden.

**Do** give a copy action the custard face once copying is the job of the moment, and drop every other control in view to quiet. On the Launcher each ready world's Copy address and each stopped world's Start are their own job, so each takes the custard face.
**Do** honour reduced motion: every animation and transition is switched off under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** keep the VIP cabinet's motion answering the Member (the Tools arriving, a pick, a press) and settling within a few seconds; nothing moves at rest.

**Do** keep the Launcher's board answering what happened (a press, a status answer): words and controls change at once and the rows follow. On arrival only the plots move, and while a world is only waiting only its busy arrow and its plot's beats do.
donts: **Don't** give cards, panels, notices or the quiet button a shadow or a coral base; depth belongs to the pressable control.
**Don't** set text in coral or custard on the seafoam field.

**Don't** fill cards or banners with custard; custard is the action and drawn light (the sun, the Minecraft plots' lights and the tabletop lamp, the VIP marquee's bulbs and the deck's pressed button).
**Don't** introduce a second line colour, gradients, or backdrop-blur glass; the world is matte and flat-drawn (the welcome's faint print grain is the only texture).
**Don't** borrow Minecraft's own art for the block motif or the plots: no logo, textures, grass or dirt colours, block faces, tools, creatures, hard offset "block" shadows or pixel fonts.
**Don't** let a plot say more than its words: no light before the backend says ready, no loop, and nothing that reads as progress while a world starts.
**Don't** use colour alone or a custard surface to say a server's state; the state is said in words, with a drawn glyph beside them.
**Don't** give the control deck's drawn buttons a custard face at rest, or anything to do; the custard Open control is the one thing to press.
